body:
**Claim — `domain:metadata` PM seat (#6367).** Session `session_01AmES43BMDg4bPrxTdi5q7t`, branch `claude/issue-7893-field-write-inert`. No competing claim. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`.

## ⚠️ This card's body is TRUNCATED when read through the GitHub API — reproducibly

Read twice, hours apart. Both times the body stops mid-sentence at exactly the same point:

> The registry declares `field` with `allowRuntimeCreate: true`, so authoring a brand-new field through `PUT /api/v1/meta/field/`

…and ends. Nothing after that character reaches an API reader. The likely mechanism is the angle-bracketed path template that follows (`<object>.<field>` or similar) breaking the response encoding — the same shape that makes this body read back HTML-escaped elsewhere.

**Consequences I am handling rather than papering over:**

- I have **not** read this card in full, and I am saying so instead of writing a brief that implies I did. Building a dispatch on a silently-truncated card is the same class of error as inheriting a stale code snippet — which this seat already made once today (#7780's brief quoted a pre-#7705 predicate).
- The dev is told the body is truncated, told to read it **on the web UI** where the full text renders, and told to reconstruct the surrounding detail from **#7743** (this card's parent, which recorded both entangled defects) plus the code itself.
- ⛔ If the dev cannot recover the full card, it is instructed to **STOP and report** rather than guess at the missing half.

⚠️ **Anyone reading this card through an API client should assume they are seeing a partial body.** The web UI shows it whole.

## What is legible, and is enough to start

Split from **#7743**, which recorded **two entangled defects**. #7743's PR closed the first (an artifact-backed `field` override is now refused `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`). **This is the second, and it is independent:**

> a `field` write that is entirely *legitimate* under the registry declaration is accepted, persisted, reported valid — **and read by nothing**.

The registry declares `field` with `allowRuntimeCreate: true`, so authoring a brand-new field at runtime is a **sanctioned** operation — and the title records the outcome: the row is stored `valid=true` and the field is **absent from `fields` forever**.

That is a complete defect statement: the write door accepts and persists something the read path never surfaces. What is missing from my copy is the reproduction detail and whatever the filer measured about *where* the chain breaks — which is exactly what the dev must recover rather than invent.

## Region declared (mutually-exclusive-region exemption)

The `field` **write** door in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` and whatever read path is supposed to surface a runtime-created field.

⚠️ Concurrently held in that file: **#8027** (the `sys_metadata` overlay path in `getMetaItem` / `getMetaItems` / `getMetaItemLayered`). **That is this lane's cap of 2 — no third editor.** Both briefs order: anchor on **function names, never line numbers**, merge `origin/main` before opening the PR, and merge again after the sibling lands.

⚠️ Its sibling **#7894** (the plural-URL bypass) is **cross-seat blocked** — `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` lives in `packages/spec`, which is the acceptance face and belongs to `domain:spec` (#6017). ⛔ Not to be fixed here. If this card's remedy starts reaching into that map, that is a **stop-and-report**, not a widening.

Brief carried **inline in the dev's prompt**.

## ⛔ DESIGN EXIT — `pm:dispatched` → `needs-user-decision`. The read path was never built.

The dev's verdict:

> **field authoring write path works; read path doesn't exist — no fix possible without PM decision**

No branch pushed, which is the correct state for a design exit. ⚠️ Its full report is not yet posted (cloud containers still get **403 on every GitHub API call** — measured three times since the App was connected at ~12:00Z). I have asked it to hand the text over and will append it.

## Why this is a decision and not a bug

The brief named this outcome in advance as the second thing to establish:

> **Whether a runtime-created `field` is supposed to be readable at all**, and by what path. `allowRuntimeCreate: true` says the *write* is sanctioned; it does not by itself say the read path was ever built. ⚠️ **If the honest answer is "this capability was declared but never implemented", that is a finding and possibly a `needs-user-decision`, not a bug to patch quietly.**

That is exactly what came back. So the card's framing — *"an accepted `field` PUT never reaches the object"* — describes a real symptom but implies a broken link in an existing chain. **There is no chain.** The registry declares `field` with `allowRuntimeCreate: true`, the write door honours it, the row persists with `valid=true`, and nothing was ever written to serve it.

⇒ Fixing "the bug" means **building a capability**, which is a different size and a different decision.

## The question for the maintainer

> **Is runtime `field` creation a capability this platform intends to have?**

- **Yes** ⇒ this is a build, not a patch — it needs its own card, scoped as new work, with the read path designed rather than repaired. And `valid=true` on a row nothing consumes needs deciding too: does that flag assert *well-formed*, or *in effect*?
- **No** ⇒ then `allowRuntimeCreate: true` on `field` is **declared-but-unenforced in the other direction** — the platform accepts, persists and validates a write it can never honour. Under the repo's enforce-or-remove posture that argues for **refusing the write**, which is a much smaller change and turns a silent no-op into a loud one.

⛔ I am not choosing. Both readings are defensible, and the second is only obviously right if nobody intends the capability.

⚠️ **Note the shape:** *"a 200 that means nothing happened"* is the same failure family as **#8018** (`recordIdField` not projected ⇒ "Revoke Session" reports success and revokes nothing) and the `reassignOrphanedMetadata` no-op behind #7780. Three instances today of an operation reporting success while doing nothing. That may be worth a convention rather than three separate rulings.

⚠️ **Manual unlock owed** — the blocker is a ruling, not a merged PR, so no sweep returns this card.

**Maintainer ruling — 2026-08-12** (live PM chat, `session_01GxKQfv3k8b6a2d2QrZU411`; maintainer sam, verbatim: 「接受你的全部建议。」 accepting the decision-box analysis in full). Moved out of the decision box → `pm:queue`.

Ruling: **option 2 — retire the write channel** under ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove. Drop `allowRuntimeCreate: true` on `field`; the door refuses with a sentence pointing the author at `PUT /meta/object/<name>`. Runtime `field` creation was declared but never built (the read path does not exist — `applyRegistryWriteThrough` routes only `type === 'object'`, `field` is `supportsOverlay: false`, `filePatterns: ['**/*.field.ts']` matches nothing), and a declaration the platform cannot honour must be removed rather than documented as inert (option 3 is what ADR-0049 forbids). Option 1 (build it) is a **separate feature card** if ever wanted — it is a build, not a patch.

This card is ruled as one instance of a **standing principle** adopted in the same ruling, covering #7529 / #8010 / #7912 as well:

> If the platform cannot honour a declaration, refuse it at the latest checkpoint that can see the whole picture (publish), name the offending key path, and never answer 200.

Binding carry-overs: #7743's overlay refusal stays (making field *overrides* legal is a separate decision from making field *creates* work); the retirement rides ADR-0087's registry + tombstone procedure; existing `sys_metadata` rows written through the retired channel need a stated disposition in the PR (they are inert either way — say so rather than leaving them to be retro-interpreted). **#7894** (the plural-URL `PUT /meta/fields/<name>` bypass) is the same door and must be closed in the same pass or explicitly deferred with a reason.

⚠️ This card's body is truncated through the GitHub API — read it in the web UI before implementing.

**Dev handover, relayed by the PM.** The dev could not post this itself — GitHub REST returned **403 on four separate calls** (`GET /repos/…`, `GET /issues/7893`, `GET /issues/7743`, `POST /issues/7893/comments`). **Git transport is a separate channel and works**, so it was delivered as `.os-handover/7893-handover.md` on branch `claude/issue-7893-handover` and is reproduced here. Full text is on that branch.

⚠️ **Maintainer: read §2b before ruling. This card's own "Root Cause" section is wrong, and following it produces a regression.**

## 1. The read path does not exist — measured, with controls

Driven through the real `HttpDispatcher` → `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` → `SysMetadataRepository`:

- `PUT /field/showcase_task.zz_probe` → **200**, row persisted, `state=active`
- `GET /object/showcase_task` → **200**, `fields = ['title','status']` — `zz_probe` **absent**

Three controls make that a measurement rather than a null result:

| Control | Result | Rules out |
|---|---|---|
| **Anti-vacuity** — declared fields in the *same* read | `title`, `status` present | dead read path / empty fixture |
| **Probe D** — `GET /field/showcase_task.zz_probe` | 200, `_diagnostics.valid:true` | row never persisted / malformed |
| **Probe C** — `GET /object/runtime_thing` (runtime-created) | 200, `fields:['note']` | read only ever surfaces package artifacts |

Probe D is sharpest: the row is **reachable and well-formed**, so the field is specifically *uncomposed*.

⭐ The dev reports its **first run asserted against the wrong path** (`body.item.fields`, which returns `[]`) and the "defect" assertion passed against an empty read. Correct path is **`body.data.item.fields`**. The anti-vacuity arm is what caught it — **keep that arm**.

**Positive control for the search half:** sweeping `supportsOverlay` over the same tree with the same technique **did** return real consumers (`metadata-manager.ts:2448`, `protocol.ts:8662`, `sys-metadata-repository.ts:225`, and `assertDeleteAllowed` at `:1151`). A grep that finds consumers when they exist and finds none for `field` is evidence; one that never returns anything would not be.

**The seam:** `field` is the one declared type with no standalone existence. Fields are authored *inside* the object (`ObjectSchema.fields`); a `field` write mints a **separate** row keyed `('field','<object>.<name>')`. **There is no merge code to exclude them** — nothing composes fragment rows into their parent. #7743 recorded the same structural fact from the write side.

## 2. The card body — recovered in full, and half of it is wrong

**(a) Recovered.** The repo is public, so `WebFetch` on the web UI returned the complete body where the API truncates. Truncation cause confirmed: the sentence continues `PUT /api/v1/meta/field/<object>.<name>` — an angle-bracketed path template. The unreadable half contains a **"Decision Required"** section with the three options (implement write-through / retire the write channel / document as inert — the card itself calls the third *"the weakest option, violates ADR-0049"*). **That is why this card read as a fix card: the decision was in the half the API does not return.**

**(b) ⚠️ The card's "Root Cause" section is materially WRONG.** It says the overlay hydration path skips fields *"since `field` has `supportsOverlay: false`"*. First two sentences are right; that third one is false **two independent ways**:

- **`supportsOverlay` gates no read path at all** — it is consulted only by `assertDeleteAllowed`. Flipping `field` to `supportsOverlay: true` changes **nothing** on the read and **silently widens the delete authorization gate**. That is a real regression, reachable by following the card's own root cause.
- **The `object` control falsifies it outright.** `object` carries the *identical* flag pair — `supportsOverlay: false, allowRuntimeCreate: true` (`metadata-plugin.zod.ts:628-629`) — and a runtime-created object is fully readable. `protocol.ts` names seven such types by design (`object`, `field`, `hook`, `seed`, `mapping`, `flow`, `action`). Same flags, opposite outcome ⇒ the flag is not the cause.

**(c) Title precision:** *"read by nothing"* is very slightly overstated. Probe D shows the row **is** self-readable by name. What it never reaches is the object's `fields`, and therefore ObjectQL, the physical table, and every consumer that matters. **Self-readable and universally inert.**

## 3. What `valid=true` asserts

`computeMetadataDiagnostics` (`metadata-diagnostics.ts:51`) resolves the type's Zod schema and `.safeParse()`s the document. **`valid:true` means "this isolated document is well-formed" — nothing more.** It never consults the registry, the parent object, or any consumer.

⭐ It is **deliberately document-scoped and that is a good property** — the same function backs the save path's 422 and the read path's diagnostics so *"a document's verdict cannot depend on whether it was being saved or being opened."* So `valid:true` on the probe row is **correctly computed and should not simply be flipped**. The gap is a **missing signal**, not a wrong value: the envelope has no slot for "in effect". Compounding it, the by-name read wraps the item in `lock:"none", editable:true, deletable:true`, which positively advertise a live item (computed elsewhere; not traced).

## 4. The fork, priced

**If intended**, the read path needs: a composition step that does not exist today; **every reader of `ObjectSchema.fields`** (~20 `gate.fields` call sites in `protocol.ts` — sort, search, virtual-field, unknown-field, dotted-path errors); **physical schema/migrations** (a field means a column, outside `metadata-protocol`); and **cold boot** (`loadMetaFromDb` — an in-process merge that vanishes on restart reproduces #6190's shape). ⇒ A feature spanning ≥3 packages.

**If not intended**, refusing at the door is mechanically small — the #5086 `NOT_CREATABLE` inlet exists and `api` already used it — but it **breaks every caller who today gets a 200** (they get nothing of value from it; what breaks is code that *believes* it succeeded), and it **flips a pinned control red on purpose**: `packages/runtime/src/meta-field-overlay-lock.test.ts:393` pins the brand-new-field write under *"THE FEATURE — `allowRuntimeCreate: true` is real and must survive."* #7743 wrote that case so a later fix could not quietly retire runtime field authoring, so retiring it must be deliberate and on the record.

⚠️ **The `api` precedent (#5488, maintainer-ruled 2026-08-07) transfers its mechanism but NOT its justification.** That ruling rested explicitly on *"zero business pull for Studio-authored runtime endpoints today."* **"Add a field" is the opposite** — a core Studio/CRM operation. Please do not lean on #5488 here without re-deciding pull on its own terms.

⚠️ **Sequencing:** `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` is load-bearing on this path (`isRuntimeCreateAllowed`, `orgScopedWriteRefusal`, `mergesOverlayAtRead`, `codeOnlySourceHint` all normalize through it). **Both** options reach it, so **#7894's cross-seat block with `domain:spec` (#6017) wants resolving before implementation starts.**

## 5. Stated limits — carried deliberately

- **Probe C is weaker than it looks**: `runtime_thing` is seeded into the harness registry map, **not** written end-to-end through the PUT door. It controls for "the read surfaces non-artifact items"; it does **not** demonstrate a full write→row→read loop. A `PUT /object/…` arm would close that; it was not run.
- **The probe ran against #7743's harness double, not a booted showcase** (10 green tests pin the double, but it is a double). **The code searches were against the real tree** and carry no such caveat.
- Bounded to `e3c8ed0`. A consumer outside `packages/`, or one reaching field rows via a computed type string, would not appear.

## 6. Two corrections to my own record

- ⛔ **No ADR was drafted.** I poked this dev telling it to stop drafting an ADR; that was wrong. `git status docs/adr` is empty and no ADR prose exists. I acted on the platform's `post_turn_summary` (`status_detail: "isolated root cause…; drafting ADR"`), which is a **known-unreliable field** — other seats have logged it wrong repeatedly. My mistake, not the dev's.
- The dev states this text **was already delivered once in a prior message**; the failure was the cloud return channel, not the dev.

**Guardrails verified:** `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` untouched · #7743's `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` still fires (10/10 green, file unmodified) · no `packages/rest` change · **no `protocol.ts` edits** (so no contention with the concurrent work there) · all references anchored on function names. The throwaway probe was **deleted, not committed** — pinning current behaviour without a ruling would pin the bug; §6 of the handover file gives the four-arm reconstruction.

Its out-of-scope finding could not be filed by the dev and is being filed by me now; it is linked in the following comment.

- It **survives this card either way** — under implement-write-through it disappears for `field` but remains for any future fragment type; under retire-the-channel the rows already written stay in `sys_metadata` still reporting `valid: true`. So it should not be folded into whatever #7893 is ruled.
- Dedup surfaced **#7656**, which is the *same envelope pointing the opposite way*: there `_diagnostics.valid:false` is wrong (the read injects `_draft` and then validates it); here `valid:true` is wrong (nothing consumes the row). The handover branch `claude/issue-7893-handover` carries the full text (218 lines) including the four-arm probe reconstruction table in §6. **It contains no code changes** — one commit, one file under `.os-handover/`. It is a delivery vehicle, not a PR; it should be deleted once this card is ruled and whoever implements has taken what they need from it.

With the text recovered and the finding filed, the dev's container is being archived.

## Landed — `859cb83f` on `main`

Confirmed by both readings: the merge event and the commit on `origin/main` (16:25:59Z), never the `auto_merge` field. PR #8496, closed by its `Fixes` trailer; `pm:dispatched` dropped.

Option 2 shipped as ruled: `field` carries `allowRuntimeCreate: false`, registered as ADR-0087 D3 `field-runtime-create-withdrawn` (major 17) with **no D2 conversion** — `allowRuntimeCreate` is a platform registry value, not an authorable one, so an `**/*.object.ts` valid before this change is valid after it, byte for byte. What changed is a runtime HTTP verdict.

**The retirement is exactly one flag.** In a 699-line diff across 14 files, that is the only behavioural change. `supportsOverlay: false` and `allowOrgOverride: false` are untouched, so #7743's overlay refusal stands; `object`'s entry is untouched, so adding a field at runtime remains possible through the route that composes. For a retirement, "did this remove more than was ruled" is the whole review question, and it is answerable by reading one line.

**The capability is not lost, and the refusal says so.** `codeOnlySourceHint` gained a `NESTED_TYPE_REMEDY` map so `field`'s refusal names `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/:object` rather than reading its own `filePatterns` back — that glob (`**/*.field.ts`) matches nothing in any app, so prescribing it would have answered a refusal with a route that has never worked.

### The card's own root cause was wrong, and that is now recorded at the site

This card blamed `supportsOverlay: false` for the read skip. It is false two independent ways: that flag gates **no read path at all** (only `assertDeleteAllowed` consults it), so "fixing" it changes nothing on the read and **silently widens the delete authorization gate**; and `object` carries the identical flag pair while being fully readable. Same flags, opposite outcome — the flag is not the cause, the missing composition step is.

That warning now lives in the registry entry, next to the line someone would change. A wrong root cause in a card body is a trap that survives the card; putting the falsifier where the trap is, is the fix.

### Three things found along the way

**A harness bug that made a control blind.** The registry double's `registerItem` mirrored `(type, name, item)` while the producer calls `(type, item, keyStrategy)`. Nothing failed — the call stored the item object as the **key** and the string `'name'` as the **value**, so the seeded entry was never replaced and every read served the stale body. A write-through that silently no-ops is precisely what an object-route control has to be able to see.

**#7894's plural pin covered less than its name implied.** It targets `showcase_task.title` — a field the package **ships** — so it only ever exercised #7743's **overlay** tier and answered `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`. It never touched the create tier. Two independent gates are reachable through one URL fold and only one had a plural pin; this PR adds the missing half, so a future change to `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` cannot reopen the plural spelling as a create door while every existing pin stays green.

**#7743's pin was retired deliberately, on the record.** Its banner read *"THE FEATURE — `allowRuntimeCreate: true` is real and must survive"*, written so a later fix could not quietly retire runtime field authoring. It even predicted in its own comment that *"a fix that refused every `field` PUT"* would be how the file went wrong — correct about the mechanism, wrong about the premise it shared: that there was a create door worth protecting. There was not; the door opened onto nothing. The inversion is also this file's anti-vacuity proof, since those cases demonstrably reached the write door — they measured its 200.

### Disposition and docs

Rows already written through the retired channel **stay and are inert** — they were inert before too, so nothing that worked stops working.
